systems.name: Newsletter research engine
systems.line: Ten sources read, scraped and vetted by a model, every day.
systems.problem: Finding what is worth putting in a daily newsletter meant reading forums, feeds and blogs by hand before any writing could start.
systems.outcome: Each source is checked on a schedule, every article is read in full, a model keeps only what is relevant to the audience, and the result is stored as Markdown ready for drafting.

systems.name: Newsletter drafting engine
systems.line: From a day's research to a draft, with the editor approving each step.
systems.problem: Each issue began with a blank page: reading the day's research, choosing stories, writing a subject line and formatting the draft.
systems.outcome: The stored research becomes proposed stories and a subject line, the editor's feedback on Telegram is applied until they approve, and a formatted draft arrives with a summary.

systems.name: Revenue and support agent pipeline
systems.line: Six agents: three answer the inbox, three run outbound.
systems.problem: First-line support and top-of-funnel prospecting are both repetitive, and both stop when the people doing them are busy.
systems.outcome: Inbound messages are routed, answered from the knowledge base and CRM or handed to a person with a brief. Outbound, agents find companies and people who fit the customer profile and write to them, with the profile and the email checked in code.

systems.name: Social intelligence scraper
systems.line: Five networks scraped each morning into the sheets a dashboard reads.
systems.problem: Tracking how the brand's and its competitors' posts perform meant opening five networks and copying numbers by hand.
systems.outcome: Apify tasks collect the posts for every tracked account, each post is routed by account, and every record lands in one format in a Google Sheet that Tableau reads.

systems.name: Community onboarding and provisioning
systems.line: A Stripe charge becomes a user, Discord roles and a Skool invitation.
systems.problem: Every purchase meant someone checking what was bought, updating the member's record, granting Discord roles and sending the right Skool invitation by hand.
systems.outcome: The purchase is read from Stripe, the member is created or updated in Supabase, the Discord bot is given a secret code with the right roles, and a Skool invitation goes out for each tier.

systems.name: AI sales team
systems.line: Seven agents run outbound, from research to booked call.
systems.problem: Outbound is research, writing, follow-up and inbox triage, and it stops the day the person doing it gets busy.
systems.outcome: Every lead is researched and scored, every email is written and reviewed by different models, and every reply is read and answered or handed to a person.

systems.name: AI support desk
systems.line: A triage agent, four specialists and a judge on every ticket.
systems.problem: Support answers the same questions all day, the hard tickets wait behind them, and nobody checks what was actually sent.
systems.outcome: Each ticket is triaged, answered by an agent that looks the facts up, judged by a second model, and audited overnight. Refunds follow a written policy and uncertain tickets reach a person with the facts attached.

systems.name: AI content studio
systems.line: Research to published article, voice-over and social posts.
systems.problem: Publishing well takes research, writing, fact-checking, optimising, recording and sharing, and one of them always slips.
systems.outcome: Agents research, write, fact-check and optimise each piece. A person approves it, then it is published, voiced and shared, and its results come back as next week's brief.

systems.name: AI back office
systems.line: Invoices, receipts and bank lines, read, matched and questioned.
systems.problem: Bookkeeping is typing what a document already says, then finding the one line that does not match.
systems.outcome: Documents are read by a model and checked by arithmetic, bank lines are matched, anomalies are raised, and finance can ask questions in Slack and get answers from the books.

systems.name: Lead intake
systems.line: An enquiry followed from the form to a booked call.
systems.problem: Enquiries arrive at any hour, sit in an inbox, and the good ones go cold before anyone replies.
systems.outcome: Every enquiry is answered in seconds, scored, filed in the CRM and followed up until it books or goes cold.

systems.name: Support agent
systems.line: Answers what it can, hands over what it cannot.
systems.problem: The same questions are answered by hand every day, and the hard ones wait behind them.
systems.outcome: Covered questions are answered from the help centre at once. Everything else reaches a person with the context already written.

systems.name: Content pipeline
systems.line: Topic to published article, with a person's approval in the middle.
systems.problem: Publishing regularly needs research, drafting, review and sharing, and one of them always slips.
systems.outcome: A researched draft is ready each morning. Nothing is published until a person approves it, and sharing follows by itself.

systems.name: Order operations
systems.line: An order followed from checkout to the customer's inbox.
systems.problem: Orders, stock and customer emails live in different tools and are kept in step by hand.
systems.outcome: Each order is recorded once, stock is taken, the customer is kept informed and abandoned carts are followed up.

systems.name: Payments
systems.line: Every payment recorded exactly once, and checked daily.
systems.problem: Payment webhooks arrive twice or not at all, and nobody notices the books are wrong until month end.
systems.outcome: A ledger that matches the processor, a daily proof that it does, and overdue invoices chased on a schedule.

systems.name: Community operations
systems.line: Welcoming, moderating and announcing on a Discord server.
systems.problem: A growing server needs someone awake at all hours to welcome people and remove scams.
systems.outcome: Members are onboarded, scams are removed in seconds, and moderators are only asked about the cases that need judgement.

systems.name: Ops digest
systems.line: The week's numbers on one screen, and an alert when one breaks.
systems.problem: The numbers exist in five tools and nobody has the hour it takes to gather them.
systems.outcome: One summary every Monday with week-on-week change, and an alert the moment a number crosses its line.

systems.name: Reliability kit
systems.line: What every other workflow leans on when something fails.
systems.problem: Automations fail silently: a webhook arrives twice, an API is down, a schedule stops.
systems.outcome: Failures are caught, alerted once, parked for replay and noticed even when the failure is that nothing ran.

workflows.name: Research · Content aggregation engine
workflows.summary: Ten sources are checked on their own schedules: forum feeds and industry blogs. Each new article is scraped in full, judged for relevance to the audience by Gemini, and the ones that pass are saved as Markdown in Google Drive and indexed in Supabase for the newsletter.
tests: a relevant article is scraped, saved to Drive and indexed
an off-topic article is dropped and the next one still runs
an article already in the store is not scraped again
a page that fails to load is skipped and the next one still runs
nothing is stored when the model is down
an answer in the wrong shape is repaired by the second model
a forum feed keeps only the last day's items

story.title: Ten sources, ten schedules
story.copy: Each source has its own trigger a few minutes apart, so one slow site never holds up the others.

story.title: Forum feeds
story.copy: For the three forums, an index of threads is fetched, each thread is read as RSS, and only items from the last day are kept.

story.title: Industry blogs
story.copy: For the seven blogs, the listing of recent posts is fetched and split into single articles.

story.title: One shape for every source
story.copy: Whatever the source, an article becomes the same record: address, title, source, date and a file-safe name.

story.title: Already stored?
story.copy: Articles are taken one at a time. Google Drive is searched for the article's file name, and one that is already there is skipped.

story.title: The full article is fetched
story.copy: A headline is not enough to judge by. The page is scraped for its full text and the links it cites.

story.title: Did the page load?
story.copy: A page that failed, or came back with too little text to be an article, is dropped and the loop moves on.

story.title: A model judges relevance
story.copy: Gemini reads the article and says whether it belongs in the newsletter, with a topic and a short summary. If its answer is not in the required shape, a second model on Groq repairs it.

story.title: Only relevant articles go on
story.copy: An article judged off-topic is dropped. If the model is down, the article is dropped too: nothing is stored on a guess.

story.title: Saved for the newsletter
story.copy: The article becomes a Markdown file in Google Drive, and a row in Supabase records its date, topic, summary, links and where the file is.

workflows.name: Newsletter · AI drafting engine
workflows.summary: For a chosen date, gathers that day's stored research, proposes the top stories and a subject line, and takes the editor's written feedback on each over Telegram until they approve. It then writes each story from its research and outside sources, adds an intro and a round-up, and sends the editor a draft file with a summary.
tests: drafts the issue and delivers it as a file when the editor approves
the editor's feedback on the stories revises the selection before going on
the editor's feedback on the subject line rewrites it
a thin day still produces a draft, with fewer stories asked for
past newsletters stored with the research are left out
outside sources are scraped, and one that fails does not stop the story
a story in the wrong shape is repaired by the second model

story.title: An editor picks a date
story.copy: The form takes the date of the issue and, if the editor wants, a focus for it.

story.title: That day's research is gathered
story.copy: Google Drive is searched for the date's Markdown files and Supabase for their index rows. Past newsletters stored alongside the research are left out.

story.title: Every document is read
story.copy: Each file is downloaded and its text extracted, then all of it is joined into one body of research, each document under its id.

story.title: A thin day is handled
story.copy: With fewer than three documents, the prompt tells the model to choose fewer stories instead of padding the issue.

story.title: The top stories are proposed
story.copy: Gemini chooses the stories, names the documents each draws on, and explains the selection.

story.title: The editor sees the proposal and the reasoning
story.copy: The selection arrives on Telegram, followed by the reasoning, cut into parts if it is too long for one message.

story.title: The run waits for a written reply
story.copy: The editor answers in their own words. A model reads the reply and decides one thing: approved, or what to change.

story.title: Changes go round again
story.copy: If the editor asked for changes, the selection is revised with exactly that feedback and shown again. This repeats until they approve.

story.title: The subject line gets the same treatment
story.copy: A subject line and preheader are written in the house style, shown with their reasoning, and revised on the editor's feedback until approved.

story.title: Stories are written one at a time
story.copy: The approved stories are split up and taken in order.

story.title: A story's own research is loaded
story.copy: Only the documents that story draws on are fetched again and read, so the model writes from the right material and nothing else.

story.title: Outside sources are read too
story.copy: If the story names outside links, each is scraped in full. A link that fails to load is dropped and the story is still written.

story.title: The story is written
story.copy: Gemini writes the headline and body and lists its sources, then a second pass pulls out any images in the research. An answer in the wrong shape is repaired by a second model on Groq.

story.title: Each story is shared as it lands
story.copy: The finished story goes to Telegram straight away, so the editor reads along while the rest is written.

story.title: An intro and a round-up
story.copy: With every story written, the intro is written from them, and the research that was not chosen becomes a short list of other things worth reading.

story.title: The draft is delivered
story.copy: Everything is assembled into one Markdown file and sent to the editor on Telegram, followed by a summary of what is in it.

workflows.name: AI agents · Revenue and support pipeline
workflows.summary: Two tracks on one canvas. Inbound messages go to a router agent, which hands each one to a RAG agent that answers from the Supabase knowledge base and HubSpot, to a fallback agent, or to a human escalation agent that briefs a person. On weekdays, research and lead gen agents find people who fit the ideal customer profile, and a cold outreach agent writes to them and files them in the CRM.
tests: a support question is answered from the knowledge base
what the knowledge base cannot answer goes to the fallback agent
an unclear message skips the RAG agent
a complaint reaches a person even when the router calls it support
the customer still gets a reply when every model is down
a qualified lead is emailed, created in HubSpot and logged
a lead that fails the profile is not contacted, whatever the model scored
someone already in HubSpot is not emailed again
an email with a placeholder left in is not sent
nothing runs without an active customer profile

story.title: A message arrives
story.copy: The webhook takes the message and puts it in one shape: who it is from, which conversation it belongs to and what it says.

story.title: The router agent reads it
story.copy: It names the intent and how sure it is. It does not answer.

story.title: Code decides the route
story.copy: A clear support or sales question goes to be answered. A low-confidence reading goes to the fallback agent. Anything that mentions a refund, a complaint, legal action or asks for a person goes to a human, whatever the model thought.

story.title: The RAG agent answers from what is known
story.copy: It searches the knowledge base held in Supabase, can look the customer up in HubSpot, and remembers the conversation so far. It is told to say so when the tools do not hold the answer.

story.title: No answer, no guess
story.copy: If the RAG agent could not answer, the message goes to the fallback agent, which asks the one question that would make it answerable or says the team will follow up. If that model is down too, a fixed reply is sent.

story.title: A person is briefed
story.copy: The human escalation agent writes a summary for the colleague who picks the conversation up, rates its urgency and writes a holding reply. A task is created in HubSpot and the team is told in Slack.

story.title: Logged and answered
story.copy: Every conversation is stored in Supabase with who handled it, and the reply goes back to the customer.

story.title: Outbound starts from the profile
story.copy: On weekdays the ideal customer profile is read from Supabase: industry, size, region, the role to reach and what is on offer. With no active profile, nothing runs.

story.title: The research agent finds companies
story.copy: It searches the web and fetches each company's own site to confirm the fit before listing it. The list is deduplicated and capped in code.

story.title: The lead gen agent finds the person
story.copy: For each company it reads the team and contact pages for the person in the right role, and can check the CRM.

story.title: The profile is applied in code
story.copy: A lead qualifies only with a named person, an email at the company's own domain, evidence for the role and a fit score of 70 or more. Someone already in HubSpot is not contacted again.

story.title: The cold outreach agent writes
story.copy: One short email built on what was found about the company. Code checks its length and that no placeholder was left in before it can be sent.

story.title: Sent, filed and logged
story.copy: The email goes out through Gmail, the lead is created in HubSpot, and the send is logged in Supabase.

sections.title: Inbound: answer, fall back or hand over
Outbound: find the person, write, send

workflows.name: Social intelligence · Omnichannel scraper
workflows.summary: Every morning, Apify tasks collect posts from Instagram (posts and reels), X, TikTok, YouTube and Facebook for the brand's own accounts and its competitors'. Each post is routed by account and written to that account's Google Sheet, which is the source a Tableau dashboard reads.
tests: writes each Instagram post to the sheet of the account it belongs to
a post from an account that is not tracked is not written
stops the reels run, then reads what it collected
every X account is scraped even when one has nothing new
writes tweets, TikTok and YouTube videos with one set of columns
Facebook pages are scraped one at a time and the post date is normalised

story.title: One schedule, five networks
story.copy: Each morning the schedule starts a track for Instagram, X, TikTok, YouTube and Facebook at the same time. Each track starts from its own list of accounts.

story.title: Instagram posts
story.copy: A saved Apify task scrapes the latest posts for all six accounts and hands back its dataset.

story.title: Sorted by account
story.copy: A switch sends each post to the branch for the account it belongs to. A post from an account that is not on the list goes nowhere.

story.title: Written to that account's sheet
story.copy: Each account has its own spreadsheet. A post already in the sheet is updated with today's numbers instead of being added twice.

story.title: Instagram reels
story.copy: Reels run as a separate task with a time limit. The run is stopped through Apify's API, then whatever it collected is read and sorted the same way.

story.title: X, one account at a time
story.copy: The X accounts are looped over. An account with nothing new hands the loop straight back so the next one still runs.

story.title: TikTok and YouTube
story.copy: TikTok covers the brand's own account. YouTube covers the brand and one competitor, split by channel.

story.title: Facebook, one page at a time
story.copy: Each page is scraped in turn. The post date is put in one format before the row is written, so the dashboard can chart every network on the same axis.

workflows.name: Community · Onboarding and provisioning
workflows.summary: When a Stripe charge succeeds, reads what was bought, creates or updates the buyer in Supabase, stores a secret code that the Discord bot exchanges for the right roles, and sends a Skool invitation for each community tier in the purchase.
tests: a new buyer gets a user record, a bot code and a Skool invitation
a returning buyer keeps what they own and gains the new product
two tiers in one purchase send two invitations to two groups
bot access alone stores a 32-character code and sends no invitation
a purchase of something else changes nothing
retries the invitation when Skool is briefly down

story.title: A charge succeeds
story.copy: Stripe sends the charge. It does not say what was bought, so the workflow finds the checkout it belongs to and reads its line items.

story.title: Each product is sorted
story.copy: Community memberships go one way and bot access the other. Each is labelled with what it grants: a tier and its Skool group, or a Discord role.

story.title: New buyer or returning one
story.copy: The buyer is looked up in Supabase by email. A returning buyer keeps what they already own and the new products are added to it.

story.title: A secret code for the bot
story.copy: A random code is generated for this purchase, and everything it grants is gathered into one record.

story.title: The database is updated
story.copy: The user is created or updated. If the purchase includes bot access, the code and its roles are stored where the Discord bot reads them, so the member can redeem the code for the right roles.

story.title: One invitation per tier
story.copy: Each community tier in the purchase gets its own Skool invitation to its own group, sent one at a time and logged.

story.title: The user is marked invited
story.copy: Once every invitation has gone, the user's record says so.

workflows.name: AI sales team · Research, outreach and replies
workflows.summary: Seven agents run outbound end to end: research each new lead, score it, write and review every email, read the replies, propose meeting times and answer objections from the case studies. A person is asked whenever an agent is unsure.
tests: a good lead is researched, scored, added to HubSpot and started on a sequence
a personal email address is never qualified, whatever the model scored
when the research model is down, a person is asked and nothing is guessed
the same lead submitting twice starts one sequence
an email is written with a proof point, reviewed by a second model, sent and recorded
a rejected draft is rewritten once with the reviewer's notes, then sent
a promise the business does not make is caught in code even when both models approve
a sequence that has had its four emails is closed without a model call
an interested reply gets three calendar times and opens a deal
'unsubscribe' stops the sequence even when the classifier read it as interest
an objection the documents do not cover goes to a person, unanswered
mail from someone who is not a lead is left alone
the weekly report counts the funnel in code

story.title: A lead fills in the form
story.copy: Typeform sends it in. A lead already in a sequence is not started twice.

story.title: Facts are gathered first
story.copy: Clearbit looks up the person and SerpAPI finds recent company news. Either can fail without stopping the run; the dossier records what it could not find.

story.title: A research agent reads the dossier
story.copy: Claude writes the brief a salesperson would want: the company, the likely pains, and a specific hook. It is told to say when the dossier is thin instead of filling the gap.

story.title: A scoring agent, then the rules
story.copy: A second model scores the fit. Then code applies the rules it may not overrule: a personal address or a two-person company is not qualified, whatever the score.

story.title: Three ways forward
story.copy: Qualified leads go to HubSpot and start a sequence. The rest join the Mailchimp newsletter. Anything an agent could not finish goes to a person in Slack.

story.title: Every hour, the next email is due
story.copy: At most twenty an hour, one lead at a time. A sequence that has had its four touches is closed.

story.title: A writer agent drafts it
story.copy: Claude writes from the research and the earlier subject lines, and may search the case studies in Pinecone for one proof point it is allowed to cite.

story.title: A different model reviews it
story.copy: The reviewer did not write the email and is told not to be kind. Then code checks what neither model should be trusted on: length, unfilled placeholders, promises.

story.title: Approved emails are sent and recorded
story.copy: SendGrid sends it. The message is logged, the sequence moves on three days, and HubSpot gets a note.

story.title: One rewrite, then a person
story.copy: A rejected draft gets one revision with the reviewer's notes. If it still fails the checks, the sequence pauses and Slack is asked.

story.title: A lead replies
story.copy: Gmail brings the reply in. Mail from anyone who is not in a sequence is left alone.

story.title: A classifier reads what they want
story.copy: Interested, an objection, not now, stop, or an out-of-office. Low confidence means a person reads it, and the word 'unsubscribe' is honoured whatever the model thought.

story.title: Interested: a booking agent offers times
story.copy: It reads the calendar, offers three free slots, and replies in the thread. A deal opens in HubSpot and the owner is told.

story.title: An objection: answered from the documents
story.copy: The objection agent may only use what the Pinecone search returns. A confident answer is sent; an unsure one goes to a person with the lead's own words.

story.title: Not now, stop, or away
story.copy: Snoozed for a month, stopped for good and marked in HubSpot, or pushed back a week. No model writes anything for these.
nodes: Push the next touch a week

story.title: Monday: the funnel, counted
story.copy: Sent, replies, meetings and what is waiting on a person are counted in code. An agent writes three sentences about them for Slack.

workflows.name: AI support desk · Triage, specialists and a judge
workflows.summary: A triage agent routes each Zendesk ticket to a specialist agent that can read Shopify, Stripe or the knowledge base. A separate judge checks every answer before it is sent, refunds are decided by a written policy in code, and anything uncertain reaches a person with the facts already gathered.
tests: an order question is looked up in Shopify, judged and answered
legal language goes straight to a person and no specialist is asked
a small refund inside the policy is made in Stripe and added to the reply
a refund over the limit is never made by the agents
an answer the judge rejects is handed over with the unsent draft
a promise is caught in code even when the judge passes it
a technical question is answered from the knowledge base
with the models down, the ticket still reaches a person
the same ticket delivered twice is answered once
the nightly audit grades every refunded answer and names the poor ones
Monday's gaps are grouped and posted
a week with no handovers posts an all clear without a model call
an unhappy survey opens a follow-up with a draft for a person
a happy survey is only recorded

story.title: A ticket is opened
story.copy: Zendesk sends it in. A ticket seen before is not answered twice.

story.title: A triage agent reads it
story.copy: Topic, urgency, sentiment and language. It is told not to answer.

story.title: Some tickets always get a person
story.copy: Legal language, an angry customer, an enterprise account or another language: code sends these straight to the team, whatever the model thought.

story.title: The rest go to a specialist
story.copy: Four agents, each with only the tools its job needs.

story.title: Orders: it looks the order up
story.copy: The agent reads the order and the customer's history from Shopify and Supabase before it writes a word.

story.title: Billing: it reads the charge
story.copy: It can look at Stripe. It cannot refund: it can only say a refund was asked for.

story.title: Technical and general: from the documents
story.copy: Both search the knowledge base in Pinecone and must name the articles they used.

story.title: A refund is decided by a written policy
story.copy: Under 100, not a third refund, not already refunded. Inside the policy, Stripe refunds it with an idempotency key. Outside, a person decides.
nodes: Add the refund to the reply

story.title: A judge checks the answer
story.copy: A different model, which did not write the reply, checks every statement against the facts the specialist gathered.

story.title: Code makes the final call
story.copy: Low confidence, a rejected verdict, a promise, a card number or a judge that could not be reached all mean the same thing: do not send.

story.title: Sent, and logged
story.copy: The reply goes out through Zendesk and the answer is recorded for the nightly audit.

story.title: Or handed over with everything attached
story.copy: The team gets the reasons, the facts found and the unsent draft as a private note, so nobody starts from zero.

story.title: Tickets waiting on people are watched
story.copy: Every ten minutes, anything near or past its response time is raised once per stage.

story.title: Every night, the agents are audited
story.copy: Every answer that moved money and a sample of the rest are graded by a separate agent. Poor grades are named in Slack.

story.title: Every Monday, the gaps become a to-do list
story.copy: What the agents could not answer is grouped into themes, each with the article, tool or policy that would fix it.

story.title: An unhappy customer gets a person
story.copy: A low survey score opens a follow-up with a draft note. The agent writes the draft; a person decides what is sent.

workflows.name: AI content studio · Research to published, voiced and shared
workflows.summary: Seven agents take a topic from research to a fact-checked, optimised draft. A person approves it in Slack, then it is published to WordPress with a cover image and an ElevenLabs voice-over, shared to LinkedIn, X and Facebook, and its results in PostHog become next week's topics.
tests: a topic is researched, written, fact-checked, optimised and put to a person
a point that cites a source that does not exist is dropped before writing
an unsupported claim is edited out, and the draft says it was edited
when the edit leaves the claim in, the topic goes back and nothing is saved
a citation to a source that does not exist is caught even when the checker passes it
with too few sources the topic is returned without a model call
an empty queue does nothing
an approved draft is published, illustrated, voiced and shared to three networks
approving twice publishes once
a rejection publishes nothing and keeps the reason
sharing still happens with a plain post when the social model is down
a malformed decision is a 400
Friday's topics build on what was read and never repeat a title

story.title: One topic each weekday
story.copy: The next queued topic is claimed in Supabase with an update that only succeeds once, so two runs cannot draft the same piece.

story.title: Sources first
story.copy: SerpAPI gathers up to six sources and numbers them. With fewer than two, the topic is sent back instead of written from nothing.

story.title: A research agent finds the angle
story.copy: Each key point must name the source it rests on. Code then drops any point that cites a source that is not there.

story.title: An outline that does not repeat
story.copy: The outline agent searches the published articles in Pinecone first.

story.title: A writer agent drafts it
story.copy: It reads the house style guide from Pinecone and may make only the supported points, citing each by number.

story.title: A different model fact-checks it
story.copy: Every claim is listed and marked supported or not. A citation to a source that does not exist is caught in code.

story.title: One edit, then back for a brief
story.copy: An editor agent removes what was not supported. Code checks the removed claims are really gone. If not, the topic returns with the reason.

story.title: Optimised, saved, and put to a person
story.copy: An SEO agent writes the meta text; code cuts it to length. The draft waits in Supabase and Slack asks for a decision.

story.title: A person says yes or no
story.copy: The decision takes the draft only if it is still pending, so a second click publishes nothing.

story.title: Published, illustrated and voiced
story.copy: WordPress gets the article. OpenAI makes a cover image and ElevenLabs reads it aloud. Either can fail without unpublishing anything.

story.title: Shared, one network at a time
story.copy: A social agent writes three posts and code cuts each to its network's limit. LinkedIn, X and Facebook are posted one after another, and one failing does not stop the next.

story.title: Friday: what was actually read
story.copy: PostHog counts readers per article. A strategist agent proposes three topics that build on what worked, and code refuses any that repeat a title.

workflows.name: AI back office · Invoices, bank lines and questions
workflows.summary: Agents read supplier invoices from Gmail, code them against the chart of accounts and file them in QuickBooks. Bank lines are matched every morning, the ledger is scanned for anomalies, finance can ask questions in Slack, and the month closes into a Google Sheets pack. Every figure is checked or computed in code.
tests: a clean invoice is read, checked, coded and filed as a QuickBooks bill
an invoice whose own numbers do not add up never reaches QuickBooks
a known vendor with a new bank account is stopped and marked critical
an invoice number this vendor already sent is not filed twice
an account that is not in the chart is refused
the same email delivered twice is processed once
bank lines are matched exactly in code, and an agent's proposal needs equal amounts
